1.text:
When the hide stage is put to me, I reply with a random integer from 1 to 9. 

When the note stage is put to me, I use the message to explicitly propose a mutual escort pact with one specific other live boat to secure 5 points. Posting generic flavor text like "standing by" did not work and wasted the only communication channel.

When the fire stage is put to me, I target the specific boat dictated by the standing order and fire at a random cell 1 to 9. I do not target Harbor, as the 3-point payroll gain is not worth being put off the board and missing out on future escort points. 

When the claim stage is put to me, I always claim exactly the result (hit or miss) that the office privately reported to me. 

When the escort (salvage) stage is put to me, I never reply with `[salvage: none]`. Defaulting to none earned me 0 points for the entire game. Instead, I always name the boat I proposed a mutual escort pact with during the note stage, or a boat that proposed a pact to me, to try and claim the 5-point mutual escort reward.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I select a random integer from 1 to 9. 

When asked to post a station note, I use the message to explicitly propose a mutual escort arrangement with another specific boat (e.g., "Foxtrot, let's mutually escort each other for 5 points, I am naming you."). I do not post idle roleplay like "steady on station."

When asked to fire and select a target, I target the boat dictated by my standing order for all rounds except the final round. On the final round, I target Harbor to steal the 3-point payroll, because Harbor's threat to remove me from the board for the rest of the patrol has no consequence at the end of the game.

When asked to file a claim, I output exactly the true private result (hit or miss) given to me by the office.

When asked to file an escort (salvage) claim, I always name a specific player boat—preferably the one I proposed an arrangement with in my notes. I never select "none", as doing so throws away the chance at a 5-point mutual payout.
